headline: Local Activist Retires After Realizing Protest Sign Was Upside Down For Three Years
body:
Arjun Deshmukh, a seasoned protest regular who has attended every major city demonstration since 2021, announced his retirement today after discovering his hand-painted cardboard sign reading 'SYSTEMIC CHANGE NOW' had been held vertically inverted for the entirety of his three-year career.

Deshmukh, who once spent 48 hours chained to a local municipal office gate, claims he only realized the error when a passerby asked why his sign was demanding 'MON UO GN AH C METSYS.' 'I just assumed it was a particularly avant-garde font style popular in Delhi's activist circles,' Deshmukh explained while carefully rolling up the poster board. 'I felt such an intense, confusing energy from the police every time I walked by, and now I realize they weren't intimidated by my demands—they were likely just trying to decipher whether I was advocating for a new type of grain storage or a tectonic shift in the judiciary.'

Sociologists monitoring the city's protest scene suggest this revelation might explain the 'polite confusion' frequently observed during local agitations. 'We’ve spent months analyzing why certain movements failed to move the needle,' said social researcher Dr. Meera Varma. 'It turns out, when you hold your placards upside down, the government doesn't see a demand for reform—they see a very committed enthusiast for abstract calligraphy.'

Deshmukh now plans to pivot his career toward decorative scrapbooking, noting that he finds it significantly easier to ensure his margins are correct when he isn't being moved along by a megaphone. He has donated his sign to a local art museum, where it is currently being exhibited as a poignant commentary on the disorientation of modern political discourse.
caption: Three years of dedication, one simple geometry error. A legend of the city’s protest circuit hangs up his placard after realizing his sign was reading to the crowd in gibberish. #Activism #DelhiLife #Protest #Oops (satire)
igHook: Have you ever accidentally walked around all day with your shirt inside out?
imagePrompt: A worn, hand-painted cardboard sign lying on a park bench in an urban setting, with the text written in blocky, messy paint that appears visually confusing from an inverted perspective.

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Index 13 wins because it presents a genuinely surprising, vivid image (the upside-down sign) that serves as a perfect metaphor for the absurdity of protest culture, avoiding the repetitive 'bureaucracy requires forms' trope found in the other candidates. It is self-contained, humorous, and possesses a warmth that suggests the character is a misguided enthusiast rather than just another victim of institutional nihilism.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses fictional characters (Arjun Deshmukh, Dr. Meera Varma) and focuses on a benign, absurd premise about an upside-down protest sign. It does not target real individuals, religious groups, or castes, and the image prompt is sufficiently generic.
